facts.claim: [Fiji, Nadi] WMO World Weather Information Service city page for Nadi (climate data supplied by Fiji Meteorological Service; station named on page only as 'Nadi'; monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990; read 26 November 2026). Mean total rainfall and rain days (days with at least 0.1 mm): March 324.0 mm, 19 rain days (mean max 31.1, min 22.6 C); July 46.0 mm, 5 rain days (max 28.5, min 18.3 C); November 138.0 mm, 11 rain days (max 30.9, min 21.5 C). The wettest listed months are January to March (299.0 to 324.0 mm) and the driest July (46.0 mm). The WMO page carries no written wet/dry season summary, only the monthly table, so no season names are stated by the source.

[French Polynesia, Tahiti] WMO World Weather Information Service city page for Tahiti (data supplied by Meteo-France; station named on page only as 'Tahiti'; temperature and precipitation are monthly averages for 1961-1990; read 26 November 2026). Mean total precipitation: January 315.2 mm and December 317.0 mm (mean max 30.3 and 29.8 C); August 48.0 mm and September 46.3 mm (mean max 28.2 and 28.6 C, min 20.5 and 21.0 C); November 162.1 mm (max 29.5, min 22.6 C). No rain-day count is given for Tahiti. The task named Papeete; WMO lists the city as 'Tahiti', not Papeete. The WMO page carries no written wet/dry season summary, only the monthly table, so no season names are stated by the source.

[Samoa, Apia] WMO World Weather Information Service city page for Apia (data supplied by Samoa Meteorology Division; station named only as 'Apia'; monthly averages for the 30-year period 1971-2000; read 26 November 2026). Mean total rainfall: January 489.0 mm (mean max 30.4, min 23.9 C); August 113.2 mm (max 29.6, min 22.8 C); November 261.7 mm (max 30.3, min 23.6 C). The lowest listed months are June to August (113.2 to 120.8 mm). No rain-day count is given. The WMO page carries no written wet/dry season summary, only the monthly table, so no season names are stated by the source.

[Vanuatu, Port Vila] WMO World Weather Information Service city page for Port Vila (data supplied by Vanuatu Meteorology and Geo-hazards Department; station named only as 'Port Vila'; monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990; rain days = days with at least 0.2 mm; read 26 November 2026). March 330.4 mm, 21 rain days (mean max 29.9, min 23.4 C); September 87.2 mm, 11 rain days (max 26.7, min 19.6 C); July mean max 25.9, min 19.5 C, 102.8 mm; November 153.7 mm, 14 rain days (max 28.9, min 21.7 C). The WMO page carries no written wet/dry season summary, only the monthly table, so no season names are stated by the source.

[New Caledonia, Noumea] WMO World Weather Information Service city page for Noumea (data supplied by Meteo-France Regional Service New Caledonia, Wallis and Futuna; station named only as 'Noumea'; monthly averages for the 30-year period 1961-1990; precipitation days = days with at least 0.1 mm; read 26 November 2026). March 134.6 mm, 17.1 precipitation days (mean max 28.5, min 22.8 C); September 39.2 mm, 9.6 days (max 23.8, min 17.7 C); July mean max 22.6, min 17.2 C, 73.0 mm; November 62.9 mm, 10.3 days (max 27.0, min 20.7 C). Noumea's listed rainfall is much lower than Nadi, Apia or Port Vila in every month shown. The WMO page carries no written wet/dry season summary, only the monthly table, so no season names are stated by the source.

[Australia, Whitsundays, Hamilton Island] Bureau of Meteorology, Climate statistics for Australian locations, Hamilton Island Airport, station 033106 (statistics for 2002 to 2026; read 26 November 2026). Mean rainfall: January 297.6 mm, February 293.3 mm, 13.2 and 14.3 days of rain >= 1 mm; August 26.4 mm, September 24.6 mm, October 27.6 mm, with 3.5, 2.9 and 3.4 rain days; November 74.5 mm, 5.4 rain days; annual 1505.4 mm. Mean maximum temperature 29.9 C in January and December, 21.6 C in July; mean minimum 18.1 C in July, 24.9 C in January. The page gives no written season summary.

[Reused from content/posts/wedding-destinations-november/03-source-pack.json fact_113, same source and checked date] [Hawaii, statewide] National Weather Service Honolulu, 'Climate of Hawai`i' (read live 26 November 2026): 'For most of Hawaii, there are only two seasons: "summer," between May and October, and "winter," between October and April.' Winter is 'the season of more frequent clouds and rainstorms', as trade winds may be interrupted by fronts, migratory cyclones and Kona storms. Hawaii's warmest months are August and September and its coolest February and March. (The page is a condensed chapter of the 1983 Atlas of Hawaii by Saul Price.)

[Reused from content/posts/wedding-destinations-november/03-source-pack.json fact_114, same source and checked date] [Hawaii, statewide] National Weather Service Honolulu, 'Climate of Hawai`i' (read live 26 November 2026): 'Hawaii's heaviest rains are come from winter storms between October and April.' When moist air rises over windward coasts and slopes, clouds and rainfall are much greater; 'Leeward areas, where the air descends, tend to be sunny and dry.' Leeward and dry areas get their rainfall mainly from a few winter storms. The NWS Honolulu page also links a 'Hawaiian Islands 2026-2027 Wet Season Outlook' (not read).

[Reused from content/posts/wedding-destinations-november/03-source-pack.json fact_101, same source and checked date] [New Zealand, one year only (November 2025), not a normal] Earth Sciences New Zealand (formerly NIWA), 'Climate Summary for November 2025' (published 9 December 2025, read live 26 November 2026), headline 'New Zealand's warmest November on record'. 'The nationwide average temperature in November 2025 was 15.9°C. This is 2.2°C above the 1991-2020 November average, making it New Zealand's warmest November on record.' The previous November record (2022) was 15.5°C. 'November began with a week-long settled spell for most of Aotearoa New Zealand, as high pressure remained slow moving nearby: a notable change after a dramatically unsettled October.' La Niña conditions continued through the month.

[Reused from content/posts/wedding-destinations-november/03-source-pack.json fact_102, same source and checked date] [New Zealand, one year only (November 2025)] Earth Sciences New Zealand, Climate Summary for November 2025 (read live 26 November 2026): rainfall was well above or above normal for most of Northland, Auckland, Waikato, the Bay of Plenty, Taranaki, southern Marlborough, Fiordland and southwestern Stewart Island; below or well below normal for southeastern Gisborne, Hawke's Bay, Whanganui, Manawatū, Wairarapa, Wellington, most of Canterbury, eastern and central Otago, and eastern and southern Southland. Low pressure systems tapping Coral Sea moisture led to 'several periods of heavy rainfall for the upper and western North Island'.

insider_details.detail: The published averages for Nadi, Port Vila and Tahiti show the first quarter carrying roughly three to six times the mid-year monthly rainfall, so for a Fiji, Vanuatu or Tahiti date between January and March plan an undercover ceremony option and a confirmed wet-weather reception space as standard, not as an extra.

Noumea's listed rainfall sits well below the other Pacific stations in every month, but its July mean maximum is 22.6 C with 17.2 C nights, so a mid-year New Caledonia evening reception needs guest wraps or heaters on the checklist.

Hamilton Island's August to October averages show fewer than four rain days a month against 13 to 14 in January and February, which matters for sail-away and beach ceremony logistics; treat summer dates as needing a fallback room booked from day one.
Apia's averages show even its lowest months above 110 mm of rain, so in Samoa a rain plan belongs in every season's booking checklist.

November sits between the extremes at most stations here (Nadi 138.0 mm, Port Vila 153.7 mm, Tahiti 162.1 mm, Hamilton Island 74.5 mm), so couples choosing late spring should be told the figures rather than a season label.
